title: microburst-queue-dampener-and-adaptive-warmup-with-kernel-hinting
author: Marisol Ortega
description: Motivation: We observed recurring microburst-induced tail spikes when the continuous batcher handled many small, bursty requests that briefly overran slot reservations. This caused KV-cache pin contention and repeated kernel warmups leading to high p99. This PR introduces a microburst dampener plus an adaptive warmup path that uses lightweight kernel hinting and proactive KV partial prefetch to smooth transient load without raising steady-state latency or cost. Design: 1) Microburst dampener queue: lightweight in-memory leaky bucket placed ahead of the continuous-batcher admission path. It absorbs sub-second bursts by smoothing admission rates per-shard and per-priority-class while preserving headroom for latency-critical requests. 2) Adaptive warmup with kernel hinting: the runtime emits a small, cheap kernel-hint request when it detects repeated short sequence workloads; the planner uses these hints to select a slightly warmer kernel path (e.g. fused attention variant) for the next N requests for that model-shard, reducing full warmup cycles. 3) KV partial prefetch scoring: a fast heuristic predicts likely KV keys for upcoming prefixes and issues low-priority prefetches that are cancelable on eviction to avoid long-term memory pressure. 4) Fairness shepherding: per-priority token buckets with decay windows to avoid starvation of low-priority streams under repeated dampening. 5) Timeouts and guardrails: configurable soft timeouts for the dampener to ensure requests are not delayed beyond SLA; automated fallback to direct admission for SLA breaches. Implementation notes: changes are isolated under runtime/continuous_batched and runtime/kernel_hints; scheduler added MicroburstDampener and WarmupHintManager; KV prefetch is an opt-in flag behind rollout config. Testing: unit tests for dampener invariants, integration harness runs comparing p50/p95/p99 against main baseline with synthetic burst traces, and a long-run soak with multi-tenant traces. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration traces - [x] internal perf run - [x] config flag and rollout plan - [x] docs note in operations guide Rollout: feature gate default off; staged rollout to non-production clusters, metric monitoring for p99 latency, KV evictions, GPU utilization, and kernel warmup count. Expected outcome: 5-12% reduction in p99 for bursty microburst workloads, negligible impact on average latency and <2% increase in tokens cost in worst case. Risks: mis-tuned prefetch can increase memory churn; warmup hints could make wrong kernel selection for rare workloads. Mitigations: conservative defaults, telemetry, and quick rollback via feature flag.

review_comments: Ethan Park: High level LGTM but let's ensure we have a fallback to bypass the dampener for SLA-exempt routes.
Marisol Ortega: Added bypass and explicit route tag checks in queue_admitter. Also added test for SLA bypass.
Priya Menon: Can the warmup hint frequency be rate-limited? Concerned about kernel thrash.
Marisol Ortega: WarmupHintManager now enforces per-shard cooldown (default 30s) and a global budget; documented defaults in experimental_flags.yaml.
Liam O'Connor: Integration run shows a small increase in KV eviction in one trace, can we make prefetch cancelation more aggressive?
Marisol Ortega: Prefetch cancelation now cancels any outstanding low-pri prefetches when memory pressure > 70% in the shard; re-ran perf suite, see CI.
ci_checks: benchmarks: pass (p99 improved on burst trace, baseline matched on steady-state)
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in microburst dampener and adaptive kernel warmup hints to reduce p99 latency on bursty, small-sequence workloads. Feature is gated behind runtime.experimental.microburst_dampener and disabled by default.
notes_for_ops: Default off. To enable in a staging cluster: set runtime.experimental.microburst_dampener=true and runtime.experimental.prefetch_scorer=true in the cluster config. Monitor metrics: continuous_batched.p99_ms, kernel.warmup_count, kv.prefetch_hits, kv.evictions. If kv.evictions spike, disable prefetch or lower prefetch_budget_pct.
related_work: This complements prior queue shaping work and the token-lease coordinator improvements; differs by focusing on sub-second microburst smoothing and kernel hint-driven warmup rather than coarse deadline-based admission.
post_merge_actions: Create a feature-rollout ticket in Linear, schedule a 2-week shadow run on non-prod clusters, and add an alert for KV eviction delta > +10% over baseline.
regression_test_plan: Add the burst_traces.yaml to the nightly perf suite for 7 days during staggered rollout; run kernel selection histogram checks weekly.
notes: Authors: M. Ortega; reviewers: E.Park, P.Menon, L.O'Connor. Followup PR planned to add telemetry UIs in the Console for warmup hint counts.
changelog_entry: runtime: opt-in microburst dampener and kernel warmup hints (Marisol Ortega)
human_summary: A targeted runtime change that smooths short bursts and reduces p99 by combining a leaky-bucket style queue dampener with conservative kernel warmup hints and cancelable KV prefetching; rolled out behind a feature flag with safety guards and observability.
